answer: Each epoch an agent's behaviour log is cut by a prism into three disjoint bands, deposited at reef anchors picked by that epoch's VRF seed. No anchor sees the whole spectrum, yet at settlement the bands must recombine into one continuous curve. A clone must reproduce continuity on every band while the cut points move each epoch, so stale replicas fail the seam check. Peers beyond the trust horizon draw random band pairs and verify seams remotely; a mismatch freezes both copies. N identities cost N full spectra plus N horizon audits, and re-cutting kills yesterday's copies.
